aiReview.summary: Official Google Skills intermediate course on Gemini, Streamlit, and Cloud Run. It is a human lab/badge path, not an installable agent skill pack, so it is a weak fit for a skills-focused directory.
evidence: Canonical URL is a Google Skills course template (paths/236/course_templates/978).
Meta description and body cover Gemini prompting, function calls, Streamlit, Docker, and Cloud Run.
Rubric prefers agent skill packs over course landing pages.
uncertainty: Exact pricing and whether labs are free without a Skills subscription.
Full lab module list beyond the marketing description.
Whether challenge-lab content is accessible without prior course progress.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on Gemini, Streamlit, and Cloud Run labs
aiReview.description: Learn Gemini prompting, Python SDK function calls, and deploying Streamlit apps as Docker containers on Cloud Run in an intermediate skill-badge course.
pros: Hosted on Google Skills with a stated intermediate skill-badge course and challenge lab.
Described scope includes text generation, Gemini API function calling with the Python SDK, Cloud Shell testing, and Cloud Run deployment.
Page lists a short duration (45 minutes) and a recent update timestamp.
cons: This is a course landing page, not a SKILL.md pack or CLI agent skill directory.
Hands-on labs typically require a Google Skills account and may not be freely usable without credits or a subscription.
No agent-installable skill files, prompts, or maintenance repo are provided on the page.

aiReview.summary: The canonical URL is a VoltAgent sponsor tracking link that redirects to SerpApi’s commercial search API homepage, not a SKILL.md pack or skill directory. Related agent skills exist elsewhere (e.g. officialskills.sh), but this candidate is a paid product landing page, not an installable agent skill.
evidence: Read of the candidate URL followed an alternate/feed path and did not serve a skill pack; search showed serpapi.com as a Google SERP API product.
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills README lists the URL as a sponsor with copy “Web Search API for your AI apps.”
README Skills by SerpApi section documents serpapi-web-search and agent-usability-test on officialskills.sh, plus GitHub tool/CLI repos, not this URL.
uncertainty: Exact current pricing tiers and free-tier limits were not verified on the live homepage.
Contents and maintenance of the officialskills.sh SerpApi SKILL.md files were not fetched.
Whether /awesome-agent-skills ever served dedicated skill docs vs. always redirecting is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Paid SERP API for structured search results in apps
aiReview.description: Provides real-time search APIs across many engines, returning structured JSON. Requires an API key; not a SKILL.md skill pack.
pros: SerpApi is a documented commercial Web Search API used by AI apps, with JSON results and many engines.
The VoltAgent list separately points to two SerpApi-authored skills (web search and agent usability test) on officialskills.sh.
Companion GitHub repos exist for Python agent tools and a CLI covering 130+ engines.
cons: https://serpapi.com/awesome-agent-skills is a UTM sponsor redirect to the product homepage, not a skill repository or SKILL.md.
The candidate is a paid API service, not an installable Claude/Codex/Gemini skill pack.
Agent usefulness of this URL is low: no skill install path, maintenance signals, or SKILL.md content on the linked page.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill for creating, editing, and analyzing Word documents via docx-js, XML unpacking, and pandoc. Directory page is thin (truncated meta copy) but points at a real GitHub skill path and install command.
evidence: officialskills.sh lists npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill docx
GitHub tree link: github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/docx
Page states support for tables, images, tracked changes, headers/footers, footnotes, TOC
uncertainty: SKILL.md completeness, tests, and last-commit recency were not fetched from GitHub
Runtime dependency quality (docx-js, pandoc) not verified here
aiReview.tagline: Create, edit, and extract Word docs for agents
aiReview.description: Install an agent skill that generates, edits, and extracts .docx content, including tables, tracked changes, headers, and TOC.
pros: Hosted under Anthropic’s public skills repo with an npx skills add install path.
Describes concrete workflows: generate with docx-js, edit OOXML, extract with pandoc.
Use cases include reports, tracked changes, markdown extraction, and TOC templates.
cons: The catalog page meta and heading text are truncated (“Handles .”).
SKILL.md body is not fully shown on the listing, so install details must be verified on GitHub.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill with a detailed SKILL.md that walks Claude through context gathering, section-by-section drafting, and reader testing for specs, RFCs, and similar docs. Installable via npx from anthropics/skills; useful for agents, not a standalone app.
evidence: canonicalUrl and GitHub tree skills/doc-coauthoring contain SKILL.md (~15KB).
Meta and page text: structured co-authoring with three stages and npx install.
Triggers include PRDs, design docs, decision docs, RFCs.
uncertainty: Ongoing maintenance cadence of the skill pack was not verified beyond current main branch.
Effectiveness of reader-testing without sub-agents was not evaluated in use.
aiReview.tagline: Three-stage workflow for co-authoring specs and docs
aiReview.description: Guides agents through context gathering, section drafting with iteration, and context-free reader tests before sharing technical docs.
pros: Official Anthropic skill in anthropics/skills with a substantial SKILL.md.
Install path is documented (npx skills add with --skill doc-coauthoring).
Workflow covers context dump, section brainstorm/curation, and reader testing via sub-agents when available.
cons: Depends on Claude artifacts, files, or sub-agents; some stages fall back to manual user testing.
Directory listing is a mirror of GitHub rather than independent documentation.

Page states workflows for extracting text, editing templates, and building decks
Source is VoltAgent awesome-agent-skills curated listing
uncertainty: Exact SKILL.md contents, license, and last-commit freshness were not fetched from GitHub
Whether the skill is still maintained in anthropics/skills main
aiReview.tagline: Read, edit, and generate PowerPoint files in agents
aiReview.description: Install an Anthropic agent skill that extracts, edits, and builds .pptx decks including slides, layouts, notes, and design.
pros: Listed as an official Anthropic skill under anthropics/skills with a GitHub tree path for skills/pptx.
Install command is given: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill pptx.
Described scope covers extract, edit, and generate presentations including layouts and speaker notes.
cons: The directory page title/meta description is truncated (“Handles everything involving .”).
SKILL.md contents are not fully shown on the listing page, so maintenance and exact APIs are not verified here.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill for reading, writing, and editing Excel/CSV/TSV with pandas, openpyxl, and LibreOffice formula recalculation. Installable via npx skills add from anthropics/skills; useful for spreadsheet work in coding agents.
evidence: officialskills.sh lists it as official Anthropic data skill with GitHub tree skills/xlsx.
Meta and body describe Excel/tabular read-write plus LibreOffice formula checks.
Install via npx skills add from github.com/anthropics/skills.
uncertainty: Exact SKILL.md contents, license, and last-commit freshness were not fully loaded.
Runtime requirements (LibreOffice, Python versions) not verified in this environment.
aiReview.tagline: Read, write, and verify Excel and tabular files
aiReview.description: Reads, writes, and edits .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, and .tsv using pandas and openpyxl, with LibreOffice recalculation to catch formula errors.
pros: Official Anthropic skill in the public anthropics/skills repo with a documented SKILL.md install path.
Covers xlsx, xlsm, csv, and tsv with pandas analysis and openpyxl formatting/formulas.
Describes LibreOffice-based recalculation to surface formula error cell locations before delivery.
Install command is explicit: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill xlsx.
cons: Directory page truncates some copy and similar-skill recommendations include unrelated Binance skills.
Depends on LibreOffice and Python libraries, which may be heavy or unavailable in some agent runtimes.
Skill body is not fully visible without expanding SKILL.md, so maintenance cadence is not verified here.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill for PDF read/write, merge/split, OCR, and related Python/CLI tooling; installable from the anthropics/skills repo.
evidence: canonicalUrl and page title identify Anthropic/pdf as an Agent Skill on officialskills.sh.

uncertainty: License, last commit, and SKILL.md completeness were not verified on GitHub.
Runtime quality of generated PDF code was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Agent skill for PDF extract, merge, OCR, and generation
aiReview.description: Maps common PDF tasks to pypdf, pdfplumber, reportlab, and CLI tools with installable SKILL.md guidance for coding agents.
pros: Listed as an official Anthropic skill with a GitHub path under anthropics/skills/skills/pdf.
Install command is documented: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill pdf.
Describes concrete operations: merge, split, rotate, watermark, encrypt, extract text/tables, OCR, and create PDFs.
Names specific libraries and CLIs: pypdf, pdfplumber, reportlab, qpdf, pdftk, pdftotext.
cons: The directory listing page is a third-party mirror (officialskills.sh), not the GitHub source itself.
SKILL.md body was not fully expanded in the fetched page, so snippet quality was not independently verified.

aiReview.description: Turns a prompt into a self-contained p5.js HTML sketch with seeded randomness, sliders, and seed navigation.

officialskills.sh documents npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill frontend-design.

uncertainty: Cannot verify how often the skill is updated or how well current CLI agents load it.

aiReview.tagline: Commit to a visual tone before generating frontend UI
aiReview.description: Guides agents to pick a distinct aesthetic first, then ship production HTML/CSS with typography, space, and motion instead of generic templates.
pros: Hosted in the official anthropics/skills repository with a SKILL.md file.
Install path is documented: npx skills add with --skill frontend-design.

Includes LICENSE.txt alongside the skill definition.

aiReview.description: Build Slack emoji or attachment GIFs from drawings or images, with easing, validation, and file-size control.

Install path is documented (npx skills add and GitHub tree URL).

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill with a SKILL.md pack that applies 10 named color/font themes (or generates a custom one) to slides, docs, reports, and HTML. Installable from anthropics/skills; useful for artifact styling, not a general coding toolkit.

officialskills.sh documents the same install command and GitHub tree URL.
Skill lists Ocean Depths through Midnight Galaxy and requires showing theme-showcase.pdf before apply.
uncertainty: LICENSE.txt terms were not fully reviewed in this pass.

aiReview.tagline: Apply 10 palettes or generate custom artifact themes
aiReview.description: Style slides, docs, reports, and HTML with 10 preset color/font themes or generate a custom theme from a description.

Names 10 themes and instructs the agent to read theme files and apply colors/fonts consistently.

Effectiveness depends on the host agent following showcase/selection steps and applying CSS/fonts correctly.

reference.excerpt:
# Modem skills

Agent skills from [Modem](https://modem.dev).

## Skills

### [`write-discoverable-code`](./write-discoverable-code/)

Rules for writing code that coding agents (and humans) can find through plain-text search: distinctive names, precise types, comments where search lands, and concept-named modules.

Distilled from Modem’s [How coding agents read your code](https://modem.dev/blog/how-coding-agents-read-your-code) post and the experiments behind it. This is skill **v4** from those runs.

## Install

Copy a skill directory into your agent’s skills folder:

```bash
# Cursor (project)
cp -R write-discoverable-code .cursor/skills/

# Claude Code (project)
cp -R write-discoverable-code .claude/skills/
```

Or clone this repo and point your harness at the skill path you want.

## Experiment data

Methodology, generated codebases, and run results live in the private [`code-writing-data`](https://github.com/modem-dev/code-writing-data) repo.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

reference.excerpt:
# Venice Skills

Agent Skills for the [Venice API](https://docs.venice.ai). Skills are self-contained folders of instructions (one `SKILL.md` each) that an LLM agent loads on demand to work correctly against a specific surface area of the API.

This repository is the canonical source of truth for Venice skills and is kept in sync with [`swagger.yaml`](https://docs.venice.ai). Use it with Cursor, Claude, Codex, Cline, or any other agent runtime that supports the Agent Skills format.

## What's in here

```
skills/        One folder per skill, each with a SKILL.md
template/      Copy this as a starting point for a new skill
```

## Skill catalog
